summary.text: Lycian in Sarpedon's host from the eddying Xanthus — inferential homeland from the collective Lycian catalogue — whom goodly Odysseus slew when Athene turned his mind toward the host; distinct from Halius the Phaeacian prince and from the Zacynthian suitor.

story.text: Odysseus smote Halius among the Lycians after Coeranus, Alastor, Chromius, and Alcandrus, and before Noëmon and Prytanis — and yet more would he have laid low had not Hector of the flashing helm strode through the foremost fighters.
